clue.text: Modesty is taken for granted within the confines of Sicily

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside the frame made by the other
the confines of a word are its boundaries, so only its first and last letters are used

parts.note: something taken for granted is implicit, understood without being stated

explanation.surface: A remark that modesty is simply assumed throughout the island of Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the confines of Sicily' gives S and Y, its first and last letters, and 'within' puts IMPLICIT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Simplicity in manner or dress is plainness without show, a close synonym of modesty.

clue.text: Divide the port

explanation.surface: An instruction to share out the port wine after dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests passing the decanter; 'the port' is really the Croatian city on the Adriatic.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide is to break apart, a synonym; and the Adriatic harbour city in Croatia bears that name.

clue.text: Churchman may virtually disregard where angels appeared overhead

parts.note: the Belgian town of Mons, where the legendary Angels of Mons were said to appear in the sky in 1914

indicators.note: virtually means almost entirely, so the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: to disregard is to ignore

explanation.surface: A cleric who might almost overlook a famous wartime vision in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' trims IGNORE to IGNOR. The Angels of Mons are a First World War legend of heavenly figures protecting British troops in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: A monsignor is a Roman Catholic priest holding an honorary papal title, so a churchman.

clue.text: Italian plane, say — well-liked but non-aristocratic tree

parts.note: the great flat region of northern Italy, plane said aloud being plain, is Lombardy

indicators.note: U is the label for upper-class usage, so being non-aristocratic means losing that letter

parts.note: something well-liked is popular

explanation.surface: An Italian aircraft that is popular with ordinary people is somehow linked to a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian plane, say' plays on plain: the Lombardy plain. 'non-aristocratic' drops U (the upper-class label) from POPULAR to leave POPLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lombardy poplar is a tall, narrow, columnar variety of the poplar, a common avenue tree.

clue.text: Videoing Prime Minister for later broadcast?

explanation.surface: Recording a head of government's speech so it can be shown on air later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for later broadcast' explains the first sense: footage 'in the can' is recorded and stored. George Canning was briefly British Prime Minister in 1827.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting film in the can means recording it for later; George Canning held the premiership in 1827.

clue.text: Barman keeps coin in small cup

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a taster is a small shallow cup used for sampling wine
P stands for a penny, a British coin

explanation.surface: A bartender stashes a coin in a little cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster is an old word for someone who draws and serves beer in a tavern.

clue.text: Narcissus about to cry

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so one letter shifts position within the word

parts.note: a narcissus grows from a bulb

explanation.surface: The vain youth of myth on the verge of tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' moves the L of BULB one place forward. The surface leans on Narcissus the self-admiring youth; here it is the daffodil family's flower.
explanation.definitionFit: To blub is informal British for to weep or sob.

clue.text: Yellow may be the answer

explanation.surface: Someone suggests the colour might be the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The answer's a lemon' is an old British catchphrase for an unsatisfactory or dismissive reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon is a pale shade of yellow; and in the idiom a dud reply is said to be a lemon.

clue.text: Vigorous growth hard to find in industry

indicators.note: to find in says one piece is located inside another

parts.note: industry or commerce is business
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A complaint that hard graft is rare in modern manufacturing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'hard to find' as 'scarce'; actually H goes inside BUSINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushiness is the quality of thick, luxuriant growth, as of hair or shrubs.

clue.text: Tennyson's work is upsetting lawyers

parts.note: upsetting someone is crossing them
the Bar is the body of barristers collectively

explanation.surface: A critic says a poet's piece is annoying the legal profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing the Bar is a short poem by Tennyson about death, which he asked to be printed last in his collections.

clue.text: Member of chain-gang who joins a television programme?

explanation.surface: A convict shackled to others who also introduces a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: A link is one ring of a chain; and a presenter connects the separate items of a broadcast.

clue.text: Rump, say, needs changing in part for Bottom

indicators.note: needs changing tells us these letters must be put into a new order

explanation.surface: A joke about a backside needing a change of nappy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream who plays Pyramus in the mechanicals' play; 'needs changing' rearranges RUMP SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's comedy the weaver Bottom takes the role of the lover in the play within the play.

clue.text: He represents a double triumph of hope over experience

definitions.text: He represents a double triumph of hope over experience

parts.words: He represents a double triumph of hope over experience
parts.note: Dr Johnson called a second marriage the triumph of hope over experience; doing that twice means three marriages

explanation.definitionFit: Someone married to three spouses has remarried twice, so twice defied experience in Johnson's sense.

clue.text: Cheerful-sounding follower of the Prophet

indicators.note: sounding says the word is chosen for how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a cheerful person is sunny

explanation.surface: A happy-seeming disciple of Muhammad.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sunni is a member of the larger branch of Islam, a follower of Muhammad.

clue.text: Air and wind eventually improved the pitch

parts.note: an air is a tune

indicators.note: eventually points to the end, so only the final letter is used

explanation.surface: A musician's song and breath control finally made the notes truer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eventually' takes D, the last letter of 'wind'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that has been tuned has had its pitch corrected.

clue.text: Inaccurate rate list can be improved

indicators.note: inaccurate says these letters are wrong as they stand and need rearranging

parts.note: a table is a list set out in rows

explanation.surface: A price list with mistakes can be put right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treatable is open to remedy, so capable of being made better.

clue.text: Easing her out, although she may have an attachment

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gently extracting a woman, even though she is clinging to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EASING HER. Attachment is the legal term for seizing a debtor's money held by a third party.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a garnishee is the person ordered to hand over a debtor's money, so subject to an attachment order.

clue.text: Voluntary fees for American prize song

parts.note: honor, spelt the American way, is a prize or award
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Gratuities paid in exchange for a US award-winning tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Honoraria are payments made for services where no fee is legally required.

clue.text: I hear you tear outside to see this dramatist

indicators.note: I hear says the words are to be judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: you rip sides, the outside of something being its sides

explanation.surface: A threat to rip someone's clothes open in order to watch a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken loosely, 'you rip sides' approximates the Greek tragedian's name, an echo of the old tailor joke 'Euripides? Eumenides.'
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian tragedian wrote Medea and The Bacchae, so a playwright.

clue.text: He dares to arrest lake polluter

indicators.note: to arrest is to seize and hold, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: one who dares or challenges is a defier
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A bold officer detains someone who has dirtied a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A defiler is someone who makes a thing dirty or impure.

clue.text: Silence's superficial companion

parts.note: in Henry IV Part 2 the country justice Silence is paired with another justice whose name also means lacking depth

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking depth is the meaning of the adjective, and Shakespeare gave that name to Justice Silence's fellow magistrate.

clue.text: It's kind to give us the low-down first

indicators.note: first places the low-down piece ahead of the other

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the low-down
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is generous to share the inside story with us before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information. 'It's kind' tempts as 'it is generous'; kind is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology and general use a genus is a class or sort.

clue.text: Plant workers have the edge

parts.note: TU is a trade union, a body of workers
a lip is a rim or edge

explanation.surface: Factory hands hold the advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory and 'edge' like advantage; the answer is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip is a spring-flowering bulbous plant.

clue.text: Take top off household cleaner and allow to drain

indicators.note: take top off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: bleach is a common household cleaner

explanation.surface: Unscrew the cap of the cleaning fluid and let it run out.
explanation.definitionFit: To leach is to let liquid percolate through, draining out soluble matter.

clue.text: Was frightened about the twisted blade

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: was frightened means feared

explanation.surface: Someone was scared by a bent knife.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowers feather an oar by turning the blade flat as it leaves the water.
explanation.definitionFit: To feather an oar is to rotate its blade horizontal between strokes.

clue.text: Debtor behind with cheque

parts.note: DR is the accounting abbreviation for debtor
aft means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone owing money pays late with a cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a written order for payment, like a banker's draft.

clue.text: Punch a drunkard's head in rough-house

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the other word

parts.note: a rough-house is a brawl

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone punches a drunk's head in a bar fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkard's head' gives D; A and D go inside BRAWL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small tool for boring holes, a punch.

clue.text: Left Debussy's score in Africa

definitions.note: the definition names a location, standing for a country there

parts.note: Iberia is a work in Debussy's orchestral Images

explanation.surface: Debussy's music was left behind on a trip to Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a West African republic founded by freed American slaves.

clue.text: Nymph is caught on the rebound

explanation.surface: A woodland spirit is captured after a broken romance.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the nymph who could only repeat others' words pined for Narcissus.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain nymph of Greek myth bears the name; and a reflected sound comes back off a surface.

clue.text: Lamb has to make things hot in pursuit of royalty

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following behind, so this piece comes after

parts.note: the crown stands for the monarchy
to roast is to cook with strong heat

explanation.surface: A lamb must chase after the king to heat things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown roast is a joint of lamb ribs tied in a ring like a crown.
